resources.string: Locks the apps you choose until you confirm it’s you

BioKey uses this service to see which app is on screen, so it can cover apps you’ve chosen to lock until you unlock them.

When you tap something on the home screen, in its search or in Recents, it reads its label, so a locked app is covered before it opens. While Recents is open and a locked app is unlocked, it reads the app names on the Recents cards, so closing that app there locks it again.

It reads the title Android gives each window, to tell Google Password Manager’s screens from sign-in sheets over other apps, and to tell which app is on screen when an app hides its screens from accessibility services. On Android 17, while Android’s own App lock prompt is up, it reads that prompt (only that window) to find the app it names, so an app you’ve locked there too asks you only once.

It can press Home or Back for you to leave a locked app you didn’t unlock, and open a locked app’s picture-in-picture window full screen so it can be covered. It can also lock the phone when you ask, after too many tries.

BioKey doesn’t read what you type, doesn’t record the screen and has no internet access. Nothing it sees or keeps leaves this phone unless you share BioKey’s diagnostic log or save a backup.
